bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeño chip beats Nvidia Blackwell on perf/watt—competitive threat crystallizing
bullets.body: OpenAI's custom Jalapeño ASIC outperforms Nvidia's GB300/Blackwell on performance-per-watt and runs level with Rubin, per Hot Chips 2026 coverage. Developed with Broadcom in 16 months vs. traditional 3-4 year tapeout cycles, analysts note 'I don't think anyone can beat this chip at perf/Watt or perf/$.' One analyst estimates OpenAI may only need 25-35% Nvidia compute by 2028, though Nvidia still must sell 10M chips to diverse customers. A separate voice notes Nvidia's durable moat remains its balance sheet and long-term supply agreements with hyperscalers.

bullets.title: NVDA options flow heavily bullish heading into Wednesday earnings
bullets.body: NVDA has the most active options flow week-to-date and showed the most bullish flow on the day. SPY is pricing only a 1/4-pt move for the NVDA earnings release vs. a 1/2-pt move for Jackson Hole, suggesting the market sees the macro event as the larger catalyst. Analysts note earnings upside reactions are being throttled until after Friday's Fed event.

bullets.title: Apple launches M6 (2nm) Mac mini and M5 Ultra Mac Studio; Evercore raises PT to $365
bullets.body: Apple surprised the market with new Mac mini (M6, M5 Pro) and Mac Studio (M5 Max, M5 Ultra) updates; M6 is Apple's first 2nm chip and features FP8 matrix ops and dual neural engines for ML. Mac mini starts at $899. Separately, Evercore ISI reiterated Outperform on AAPL and raised its price target to $365, citing the AI Mac expansion.

bullets.title: Goldman credit desk flags NVDA/AVGO CDS widening—credit questioning AI financing backstops
bullets.body: Goldman's Delta-1 head noted NVDA and Broadcom CDS widening as credit markets raise questions about AI financing structures and the sustainability of AI capex, a concern equity markets have not yet fully incorporated. Goldman headline: 'The AI Story Is Not Dead But Goldman Warns Credit Is Asking Questions That Equity Markets Aren't.'

bullets.title: Memory poised to capture 68% of CSP capex next year; memory suppliers 'eating all the CAPEX'
bullets.body: TrendForce forecasts memory will account for 68% of cloud service provider capex next year as the 'Bank of Memory controls everything.' One analyst argues Nvidia has lost its performance-per-dollar and performance-per-watt crowns post-2025, with memory suppliers now capturing the bulk of AI infrastructure spend. Samsung LPDDR integration with compute for inference adds to the memory-centric trend.

bullets.title: $3M+ unusual bullish options prints detected in MU and AMD
bullets.body: Unusual bullish options flow of $3M+ each detected in both Micron and AMD on the session, consistent with the broader semiconductor options activity spike heading into NVDA earnings.

bullets.title: INTC x86 share falls below 70% in Q2 2026 as AMD hits record high
bullets.body: Intel's x86 market share dropped below 70% in Q2 2026 for the first time, a 'significant erosion,' while AMD reached a record high share driven by competitive processors and AI infrastructure demand. Custom ASIC design services also seen as a growing opportunity for AMD and INTC to compete for hyperscaler chip dollars.

bullets.title: Waymo begins autonomous vehicle testing in Munich, expanding international footprint
bullets.body: Google subsidiary Waymo announced it will begin autonomous vehicle testing in Munich, Germany in the coming weeks, marking its first European testing expansion.

bullets.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise for legal and financial services with new partnerships
bullets.body: Google Cloud unveiled Gemini Enterprise AI targeting legal and financial services, announcing partnerships with Weil Partners, Moody's, MSCI, Relativity, and others. Product launch broadens Google's enterprise AI footprint against Microsoft/OpenAI.

bullets.title: Anthropic claims $30T+ TAM to investors; IPO reportedly in coming months
bullets.body: WSJ reports Anthropic is expected to tell investors its potential revenue opportunity exceeds $30 trillion—surpassing SpaceX's prior $28.5T TAM claim—ahead of a reported IPO. Polymarket assigns 74% odds of Anthropic releasing its next Mythos-class model by September 9. One skeptic notes token prices are cratering and the $2T valuation needs a Mythos 2 launch to justify it.

bullets.title: Canada retaliates with 15-50% tariffs on $20B of US goods, effective Sept. 8
bullets.body: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on approximately $20 billion of U.S. products including steel (doubled to 50%), aluminum, dairy, appliances, motorcycles, and farm equipment, effective September 8. UBS cut its 2026 Canada GDP growth forecast to 0.9% and Canada signals little chance of resuming trade talks before U.S. midterms.

bullets.title: US macro data soft: Consumer Confidence 89.4 (7-month low), New Home Sales -10.5% m/m
bullets.body: August CB Consumer Confidence fell to 89.4 vs 90.2 estimate and prior 90.2, with the expectations component dropping sharply to 68.2 from 74.0. June new home sales collapsed 10.5% m/m vs. -1.4% estimate; median new home prices hit a 5-year low. Richmond Fed Manufacturing missed at +4 vs. +7 est. The present-situation component of confidence was the sole bright spot at 121.2.

bullets.title: Treasury 2Y auction strong: 4th consecutive stop-through, highest foreign buying since March 2025
bullets.body: The $69B 2-year Treasury auction stopped through by 0.4bps (WI 4.208%, yield 4.204%), marking the fourth consecutive stop-through. Foreign buying hit its highest level since March 2025. 10-year yields fell 6bp to 4.64% on the session.

bullets.title: Fed's Collins hawkish: rate hike 'appropriate soon' absent sustained disinflation
bullets.body: Boston Fed President Susan Collins called June and July inflation data 'mildly encouraging' but said it would be 'appropriate to raise interest rates soon' absent evidence of sustained disinflation. Collins noted rising long-term rates should work against re-acceleration in demand and that inflation remains 'too high.'

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz: mines cleared per Trump; Oman-Iran propose temporary shipping corridor
bullets.body: Trump announced the US Navy removed/detonated all mines from the Strait of Hormuz and warned Iran any new mine placement would result in destruction of the vessel. Separately, Oman and Iran discussed a phased plan including a temporary joint shipping corridor and mine clearance. Polymarket implies sub-10% probability of normalized Hormuz traffic by year-end.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole looms: markets pricing twice as much move for Fed than for NVDA earnings
bullets.body: A fintwit options analyst notes the market is pricing a 1/4-pt SPY move for NVDA earnings Wednesday vs. a 1/2-pt move for Jackson Hole Friday, suggesting macro uncertainty is dominating. Bespoke Morning Note flags the VIX hovering near historic August lows even as QQQ trades 1% below its 50-DMA and is down 3.2% over the past week.

bullets.title: Market breadth rotation: RSP +7% vs SPX +1.8% since May; semis holding while broader market fades
bullets.body: Equal-weight S&P (RSP) has outperformed cap-weight SPX by ~5.2pp since May, signaling broad market strength vs. mega-cap concentration risk. One session observation: semis ($SOXX) held up while the broader market sold off at the open, with equal-weight variants furthest above their 50-DMAs.

bullets.title: AMZN raising AI device prices amid chip supply constraints; cloud/AI players forced to raise equity
bullets.body: Amazon is increasing prices on AI devices due to chip supply constraints, shifting customers toward rental models. More broadly, major cloud/AI players are now raising equity capital for AI infrastructure despite strong cash generation, suggesting capex needs have exceeded self-funding capacity.

bullets.title: NBIS: ClickHouse ARR surpasses $350M; Nebius owns 28% stake
bullets.body: ClickHouse's annual recurring revenue exceeded $350 million, a notable milestone for the Nebius-owned (28% stake as of May 2025) database platform. The figure was highlighted on X as a positive catalyst for NBIS shares.

bullets.title: Paramount execs signal openness to structural remedies in AG lawsuit; WBD partnership still needed
bullets.body: Paramount executives publicly acknowledged willingness to accept structural remedies for the first time in the AG lawsuit context, with the company stating it remains hopeful and ready for good-faith discussions to keep the transaction on track. Separately, analyst commentary notes Ellison's Google-recruited talent rebuilding Paramount+ still needs Warner Bros/HBO content to be competitive.
